items.stem: Which best describes what SDM is?

options.text: An automated tool that syncs data between HR, Entra, AD, and SharePoint
An admin portal where authorized people make the authoritative edits to district data
A reporting dashboard for viewing district data
The District Data Hub (DDH) database itself

items.explanation: SDM is the human-editorial portal: people make the authoritative edits that the Sync-* fleet then propagates.

misconceptions.a: That's the Sync-* family's job — mechanical reconciliation. SDM is where humans make the editorial calls.
misconceptions.c: SDM is for editing the authoritative record, not just viewing reports.
misconceptions.d: DDH is the database SDM edits; SDM is the app on top of it.

items.stem: Where does SDM sit relative to the Sync-* fleet and DDH?

options.text: Syncs load DDH → humans edit in SDM → syncs propagate the edits outward
SDM loads DDH first, then the syncs let humans edit it
SDM replaces the syncs entirely
SDM only runs after all syncs are disabled

items.explanation: SDM is the editorial layer in the middle: bulk data loads into DDH, humans correct/extend it in SDM, and the Sync-DDH-* fleet carries the result out to AD/Entra/SharePoint.

misconceptions.b: Humans edit the data that already lives in DDH; SDM doesn't do the bulk load.
misconceptions.c: SDM complements the syncs — it doesn't replace their mechanical reconciliation.
misconceptions.d: SDM and the syncs operate together, not mutually exclusively.

items.stem: Which of these does a person actually do in SDM? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Augment or correct the supplemental data on an existing school
Create a brand-new school or delete one
Fix a standalone group's membership
Add a temporary job or contractor that HR doesn't manage
Run the nightly mechanical reconciliation of HR into DDH

items.explanation: SDM augments/corrects the supplemental data on records the syncs source (like schools) and maintains the things it owns (standalone group membership, HR-gap staffing such as temp jobs and contractors). It does NOT create or delete system-of-record entities like schools — those come from the source system via the syncs — and it doesn't run the syncs.

misconceptions.b: Schools are sourced from a system of record; SDM augments a school's data but cannot create or remove the school itself.
misconceptions.e: That bulk, scheduled reconciliation is the Sync-* fleet's job, not a human action in SDM.

items.stem: A new teammate says: "SDM is just one of the sync tools — it moves data between systems on a schedule." Correct them in two or three sentences.
rubric: Identifies the misconception: SDM is not an automated sync; the Sync-* family does the mechanical movement
States what SDM actually is: the portal where authorized humans make authoritative edits to district data (DDH)
Optionally notes the flow: those edits then propagate outward via the syncs
items.sampleAnswer: Not quite — the mechanical, scheduled movement between HR, Entra, AD, and SharePoint is the Sync-* fleet's job. SDM is the opposite: it's the admin portal where authorized people make the authoritative editorial changes to the district's data in DDH, and the syncs then carry those changes out to the other systems.

items.stem: The name "Supplemental Data Manager" points at its core job. What does SDM primarily manage?

options.text: A backup copy of everything already in DDH
System-of-record sources, augmented with supplemental data that downstream apps need but DDH itself doesn't hold
Only the look-and-feel settings of the sync tools
The HR system's master staff records

items.explanation: SDM's core role is to manage system-of-record sources and augment them with the extra data downstream consumers require that DDH doesn't carry — the "supplemental" in the name.

misconceptions.a: SDM isn't a backup — it manages data DDH doesn't hold, not a copy of what DDH already has.
misconceptions.c: It manages real district data (and the sync config), not just UI settings.
misconceptions.d: HR remains the system of record for the staff it manages; SDM fills the gaps HR doesn't cover.

items.stem: SDM is designed around a RACI self-serve model. What does that mean in practice?

options.text: A central IT team keys in every change on users' behalf
Editorial responsibility sits with the people who own the data, who maintain it themselves
Every change needs manager sign-off before it can be saved
The syncs decide who is allowed to edit each record

items.explanation: The RACI self-serve model puts editing in the hands of the data owners (the data-owners team and delegated school staff) rather than a central team.

misconceptions.a: That's the opposite of self-serve — the point is the owners do their own edits.
misconceptions.c: There's no universal sign-off gate; ownership is distributed to the data owners.
misconceptions.d: Authorization is AAD-group-driven, but the self-serve model is about who does the editing, not the syncs.

items.stem: As SDM evolved, its scope widened beyond editing DDH entities. Which of the following did it take on? Select all that apply.

options.text: The volatile template/configuration JSON files that drive the syncs
Staffing categories HR doesn't manage — temporary jobs under six weeks, contractors, and vendors
Running the mechanical nightly sync reconciliations itself
Becoming the system of record for all HR staff data

items.explanation: Over time SDM absorbed the sync template/config JSON and the HR-gap staffing categories (temp jobs under six weeks, contractors, vendors). It still doesn't run the syncs, nor does it replace HR as the staff system of record.

misconceptions.c: The Sync-* fleet runs the reconciliations; SDM manages the data and config, not the sync execution.
misconceptions.d: HR remains the system of record for the staff it manages; SDM only covers the gaps.
